findings.note: THE DOCUMENTED INSTALL INSTRUCTION CANNOT RESOLVE THE PACKAGE IT IS PRINTED IN, and it is family-wide rather than a typo. rust-ai-native README:15 says: Require `stack:org.vibevm.ai-native/rust-ai-native` (`^0.6`) to get the whole family - while that package's own vibe.toml is version = "0.7.0". Under caret semantics for 0.x, ^0.6 means >=0.6.0 <0.7.0, so it EXCLUDES the very version shipping the sentence. typescript-ai-native has the identical defect one minor down: README:16 says ^0.5, vibe.toml says 0.6.0. go-ai-native (v0.1.0) carries no such line. Both offenders are EXACTLY one minor behind their own version, which is the signature of a mechanical version bump that did not touch the prose - the same class as wave 1's stale status lines, but worse, because a status line misleads a reader while this one misconfigures a consumer. Found in the FIRST aggregator file opened during the Phase A pilot. Fix direction: the caret in an aggregator README is derived data - it should be generated from, or gate-checked against, the manifest version, because a family aggregator's whole job is to name a version set and it bumps on every release.

PREDICTION 2 CONFIRMED AT THE PILOT, and concretely. The plan predicted the aggregator genre would need at least one grammar amendment to PROP-043 3.8. The umbrella packages are content-minimal by design (PROP-028): rust-ai-native carries a 19-line README and a manifest, and THREE OF ITS FOUR SUBSTANTIVE FACTS ARE ABOUT OTHER PACKAGES - what rust-ai-native-lang ships (GUIDE, cards, toolchain), what rust-ai-native-mcp serves, that core-ai-native arrives transitively. Marking those `@impl/done` here asserts, in this document, something this document cannot be the source of truth for: the truth conditions live in another package, and when that package changes nothing here notices. Wave 1 never hit this because a host PROP owns its own subject matter. The grammar needs a way to say `this fact is ABOUT <other unit>` - a borrowed or delegating anchor whose verdict is derived from the owning unit's rather than asserted independently, so a stale aggregator is detected by the owner moving rather than by someone re-reading the aggregator. Until that exists, the honest fallback is to mark such facts `unverifiable` in the aggregator and verify them where they live.

THE EXHAUSTIVE COUNTER DEMANDS FACT MARKUP ON VERBATIM LICENCE BOILERPLATE. Measured at the Phase A pilot 2026-07-26: `progress check --exhaustive` reports 8 992 unmarked paragraphs across the widened scope, and 264 of them (3%) live in 33 LICENSE.md files - the same UPL-1.0 text copied once per package version slot. Marking them would mint ~264 fact anchors on someone else's words, 33 times over, and every one of them would be a fact this project is not the author or the source of truth for. Wave 1 never hit this because spec/ carries no LICENSE files. The precedent already exists and points the right way: DEFAULT_EXCLUDES (scope.rs:11-20) already drops `refs` as third-party and `fixtures` as not-a-contract, always-on and even under an explicit include. LICENSE.md is the same category. FIX DIRECTION: add it to DEFAULT_EXCLUDES rather than to progress.toml - section 4 is include-only BY DESIGN ('exclusions are expressed by enumeration'), so there is no config-side way to express this and it needs a small code change plus a test. Until then the Phase B exit gate (`check --exhaustive` green over both corpora) cannot be reached honestly: either 264 boilerplate paragraphs get marked, or the gate stays red for a reason nobody should have to re-derive.

THREE DERIVED FILES ARE IN THE OBSERVED SCOPE AND MUST NOT BE. Found 2026-07-26 on an owner challenge to prove nothing generated had been let in. `spec/cards/INDEX.md` in all three language stacks (rust v0.7.0, typescript v0.6.0, go v0.1.0) says of ITSELF, verbatim: 'Generated/maintained as a derived index (A2/R-030); hand edits are a defect.' Marking them is by their own words a defect, and any markup written there dies on the next regeneration - exactly the reason wave 1 put spec/boot/STATIC.md and spec/boot/INDEX.md out of scope (progress.toml, owner ruling 2026-07-24). Wave 1 expressed that exclusion through its include glob `spec/boot/[0-9]*.md`, which drops unnumbered files naturally; `packages/**/*.md` has no such trick and section 4 is include-only by design, so this needs the same code-side fix surface as F-070. VERIFIED CLEAN in the same sweep, so nobody re-audits it: across all 344 observed files there are exactly two top-level roots (`packages`, `spec`) and NO path segment named target, vibedeps, node_modules, vendor, .vibe, refs, campaigns, fixtures, dist, build, generated or .git - DEFAULT_EXCLUDES (scope.rs:11-20) holds those, always-on and even under an explicit include. A first sweep for 'generated/do not edit' phrasing returned 11 files and ALL ELEVEN WERE FALSE POSITIVES - documents ABOUT generated code (the Go/Java/Kotlin guides' generated-code rule, scaffold-a-generators describing the `// Code generated ... DO NOT EDIT.` marker, git-attribution-policy discussing 'generated by' trailers, managed-blocks describing do-not-edit notices, wal-status instructing a reader not to edit the WAL). The three real ones use different wording entirely ('derived index'), which is why a phrase-matching sweep alone is not a safe audit for this.
